review_notes: I read the whole target file. I compared it with the sibling files Dihedral/Three.lean and QuaternionEight.lean, and with Rational/Solver.lean, Rational/Basic.lean and Dixon/ExactChecker.lean. The `fin_cases ... <;> decide` blocks are short routine checks and I did not report them. Two multi-step assembly proofs are repeated verbatim, up to renaming, in at least three files. One is the tail of the solver-success theorem. The other is the Nat.card-to-Fintype.card adaptation of the spec fields. I did not run Lean, so the proposed helpers are untested. The second helper needs a generic group `G` with `Fintype G` and `DecidableEq G`, as `ClassData` already assumes. The first helper's `p` hypothesis follows `isSome_dixonRationalCharacterTable_iff`.

findings.problem: The proof turns the lifted-rows equation into row membership and then builds the existential witness. The same steps appear in `isSome_dixonRationalCharacterTable_dihedralGroupThree` and `isSome_dixonRationalCharacterTable_quaternionGroupTwo`. Each copy differs only in the group name. Nothing in the proof is specific to the dihedral group. The logic is: if `liftedCentralRows p = univ.image omega` and `(omega, table, degree)` satisfies the integer spec, then the solver succeeds. That reasoning is rebuilt in every group file.
findings.proposed_change:
Add to Rational/Solver.lean, next to `isSome_dixonRationalCharacterTable_iff`:

theorem isSome_dixonRationalCharacterTable_of_liftedCentralRows_eq (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] {omega table : Matrix (Fin d.numClasses) (Fin d.numClasses) ℤ} {degree : Fin d.numClasses → ℕ} (hrows : d.liftedCentralRows p = Finset.univ.image fun i => omega i) (hspec : d.IsIntegerCharacterTableSpec omega table degree) : (d.dixonRationalCharacterTable? p).isSome = true.

Proof: `rw [d.isSome_dixonRationalCharacterTable_iff]; refine ⟨⟨omega, table, degree⟩, fun i => ?_, hspec⟩; rw [hrows]; exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨i, Finset.mem_univ i, rfl⟩`.

The target proof becomes `isSome_dixonRationalCharacterTable_of_liftedCentralRows_eq _ _ dihedralGroupFour_liftedCentralRows isIntegerCharacterTableSpec_dihedralGroupFour`. The Three, QuaternionEight and CyclicTwo files use the same one-liner with their own `liftedCentralRows` and spec theorems.
findings.benefit: The solver-success argument is stated and proved once, next to the iff it comes from. Each per-group file then only supplies its two certificates, `liftedCentralRows` and the spec. If the shape of `IntegerCharacterTableData` or the iff changes, one proof needs updating instead of one per group file.

findings.problem: The supporting lemmas (`_characterDegrees_pos_and_dvd`, `_sum_characterDegrees_sq`, `_characterTable_orthogonal`) are all stated with `Nat.card (DihedralGroup 4)`. The spec structure uses `Fintype.card G`. So the spec proof has to convert between the two with `simpa only [Nat.card_eq_fintype_card, Nat.cast_ite, Nat.cast_zero]`. The same conversion and field-by-field assembly appear in `isIntegerCharacterTableSpec_dihedralGroupThree` and `isIntegerCharacterTableSpec_quaternionGroupTwo`. Each file also states these `Nat.card` lemmas only to convert them again, and each starts the proofs with `rw [DihedralGroup.nat_card]` or a similar rewrite.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one constructor lemma next to the spec definition, for example `ClassData.IsIntegerCharacterTableSpec.of_natCard`. Its hypotheses are `central_one`, `central_eigen`, `degree_pos`, `degree_dvd` and `sum_degree_sq`, the last two stated with `Nat.card G`. It also takes `degree_mul_central`, and `row_orthogonal` with `if i = j then (Nat.card G : ℤ) else 0`, matching the file's existing orthogonality lemma. The proof is `simpa only [Nat.card_eq_fintype_card, Nat.cast_ite, Nat.cast_zero]` applied once to each of the three affected fields. The target theorem then reduces to `.of_natCard (by intro i; fin_cases i <;> decide) isModularEigenrow_..._int (fun i => (…pos_and_dvd i).1) (fun i => (…pos_and_dvd i).2) …sum_characterDegrees_sq …degree_mul_centralCharacterTable …characterTable_orthogonal`.

Alternatively, restate the per-group lemmas with `Fintype.card` and drop the conversions. Either way the Nat.card-to-Fintype.card plumbing exists in one place.
findings.benefit: The three or more group files no longer carry the same field-by-field conversion boilerplate. A reader sees only the group-specific facts. A future change to the spec fields is fixed in one lemma.

findings.problem: Two theorems repeat the same pipeline in `Three.lean` and `QuaternionEight.lean`, and in this file. The first is `centralCharacterSearch_eq_rowsOfMap_of_isGoodDixonPrime` followed by the `(by intro i; fin_cases i <;> decide)` normalization check, then the integer-to-ZMod eigenrow transport, then a card hypothesis. The second is `liftedCentralRows_eq_image_of_centralCharacterSearch_eq` followed by a `fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> decide` bound check on `2 * natAbs < p`. In each file the second theorem is also proved from the first. Both are then repeated for every group. The `rw [← …DihedralPrimeData_p] at hcard` step exists only to bridge the literal `5` and `p`, so it is bookkeeping and not mathematics.
findings.benefit: Every group file would shrink to its genuinely specific data. The argument that a reduced integral table recovers the whole search and the lifted rows would be stated once. It also removes the `ZMod 5` versus `p` rewriting that each file has to handle by hand.
